body.objective: Add a fail-closed operator-domain and boundary-form calculus. Current exact algebra can compare differential expressions, but the black-hole, causal and quantum programmes require the stronger distinction between an expression, a closed operator with a declared domain, and a self-adjoint/Fredholm realization under boundary conditions. Conflux must not identify two operators or determinants when their domains, endpoint data or boundary pairings differ.
body.stop_condition: Define typed differential expressions, graph domains, maximal/minimal realizations, formal and Hilbert/Krein adjoints, Green boundary forms, trace maps, boundary relations and boundary triples. Implement exact finite endpoint deficiency counts, Lagrangian boundary subspaces, self-adjoint/symmetric extension checks, Fredholm kernels/cokernels/index, relative index and spectral-flow bookkeeping for declared finite reductions; connect validated ODE enclosures to endpoint maps without promoting numeric evidence to exact. Demonstrate on a regular Sturm-Liouville fixture and the declared axial Schwarzschild radial system: distinguish identical differential expressions with inequivalent boundary conditions, reconstruct the horizon/infinity boundary pairing, determine whether a candidate endpoint class defines a closed finite-flux realization, and either certify or refuse the claimed Einstein/additional quotient. Export domains, trace spaces, boundary relations, indices and unresolved analytic hypotheses to Conflux as non-erasable types.
body.forbid: no differential expression treated as an operator without a domain; no formal adjoint treated as a Hilbert-space adjoint; no bounded leading term treated as finite flux; no self-adjointness inferred from a symmetric matrix fixture alone; no numerical nullity called an exact deficiency index; no determinant or spectrum compared across unequal domains; no general infinite-dimensional Fredholm theorem claimed from a finite reduction
notes: Priority A for black-hole and Lorentzian quantum adoption.
Compose with support-wavefront-green-kernel, validated-vector-bvp, spectral-resolvent and exact symplectic boundary data.
The first slice should be a typed theorem ledger plus exact/validated endpoint reductions, not an attempt to formalize all functional analysis.
